newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-REFORMED BAIANO COULD BE A KEY PLAYER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REFORMED BAIANO COULD BE A KEY PLAYER.

text.p: Junior Baiano, a player with a "bad boy" reputation in Brazil, is now being tipped as the answer to the national team's defensive problems.

The Flamengo defender was acclaimed as Brazil's most impressive performer during this week's two-match tour to the Far East where the world champions clocked up their eighth and ninth successive victories.

He looked at ease in the famous gold shirt from the moment he came on at halftime for his international debut in Sunday's game against South Korea, where Brazil scored twice in the last 10 minutes to win 2-1.
An equally imposing performance followed against Japan on Wednesday, crowned by his headed final goal in a 3-0 victory.
"I told him, no messing around or violence. The national team is a serious business," coach Mario Zagallo said in the Jornal do Brasil newspaper. "In the end, he surprised me."
Brazil's defence had been a worry before the tour, especially after leaking four goals in a 4-2 friendly defeat away to Norway and a further three in a draw with Italy.

Zagallo has chopped and changed the central defensive pairing but none of his combinations has looked convincing and critics believed the decision to pick Junior Baiano for the Asia tour was that of a desperate man.
After all, it was not long ago that he was thrown out of German club Werder Bremen for punching an opponent.
In his first spell at Flamengo he had been involved in a number of notorious incidents, the most infamous when television cameras caught a close-up of him off the ball elbowing an opponent.
Zagallo's gamble, however, appears to have paid off.
Other high points of the tour were the performances of midfielder Flavio Conceicao, who scored with two spectacular long-range efforts against Japan, and striker Sonny Anderson.

Anderson, who has just joined Barcelona to replace compatriot Ronaldo, was finally rewarded after years of impressive performances for French club Monaco and replied by scoring the winner against South Korea just 15 minutes into his debut.
The low point was the theatrical tactics employed by Ronaldo to win the penalty from which he equalised against South Korea.
Television replays clearly showed that the world's most expensive player was untouched by anyone as he tumbled over in the penalty area.
Zagallo was also angry to discover that midfielder Rivaldo, who pulled out of the tour through injury, played for his Spanish club side Deportivo Coruna in a pre-season friendly on Tuesday.
